verses.commentary: What misery is mine! Like one gathering summer fruit at gleaning time: no cluster of grapes, no early figs that I crave. The prophet laments. Searching for righteousness like searching for fruit after harvest. Nothing remains. Goodness depleted.

The faithful swept from the land. Not one upright person remains. Everyone lies in wait to shed blood; they hunt each other with nets. Total moral collapse. Faithfulness extinct. Humanity becomes predatory. The neighbor is the enemy.

Both hands skilled in doing evil. The ruler demands gifts, the judge accepts bribes, the powerful dictate what they desire. They all conspire together. Bimanual competence in corruption. Government, judiciary, and power brokers collude. Conspiracy of wickedness.

The best of them is like a brier, the most upright worse than a thorn hedge. The day God visits has come, the day your watchmen sound the alarm. Now is the time of confusion. Even the best are harmful. Upright people scratch and tear. Judgment arrives. Watchmen warned. Confusion descends.

Do not trust a neighbor; put no confidence in a friend. Guard the words of your lips from the woman who lies in your embrace. Social trust destroyed. Friends betray. Intimacy becomes danger. Even pillow talk risks exposure.

Son dishonors father, daughter rises against mother, daughter in law against mother in law. A man's enemies are members of his own household. Jesus quotes this (Matthew 10:35-36). Family bonds broken. Home becomes hostile. Domestic warfare.

But as for me, I watch in hope for the Lord. I wait for God my Savior; my God will hear me. Personal confession amid social collapse. Hope despite circumstance. Waiting as spiritual discipline. God hears even when humans betray.

Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the Lord will be my light. Defiant faith addressed to oppressor. Fall is not final. Darkness is not permanent. Divine light penetrates.

Because I have sinned against him, I will bear the Lord's wrath until he pleads my case and upholds my cause. He will bring me into the light; I will see his righteousness. Sin acknowledged. Wrath accepted as just. But wrath has an end. Vindication follows discipline.

Then my enemy will see it, covered with shame. She who said: Where is the Lord your God? My eyes will see her downfall; she will be trampled like mire in the streets. Mocking question reversed. The enemy who taunted becomes the enemy who is shamed. Roles reverse.
The day for building your walls will come, the day for extending your boundaries. Restoration announced. Walls rebuilt. Expansion resumes. Constriction gives way to growth.

In that day people will come to you from Assyria and Egypt's cities, from Egypt to the Euphrates, from sea to sea, from mountain to mountain. Universal ingathering. Former oppressors (Assyria, Egypt) become pilgrims. Geography spanned. Borders abolished.
The earth will become desolate because of its inhabitants, as result of their deeds. Judgment on the nations before blessing. Deeds produce desolation. What one sows, one reaps.

Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock of your inheritance, which lives alone in a forest, in fertile pasture. Let them feed in Bashan and Gilead as in days of old. Prayer for divine shepherding. Rich pasturelands named. Restoration to ancestral abundance.
As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show them my wonders. God responds. A new exodus promised. What was, will be again. Ancient wonders repeated.

Nations will see and be ashamed, deprived of all their power. They will put hands over their mouths, ears will become deaf. Gentile nations silenced and deafened. Power stripped. Boasting ends. Humiliation before displayed divine power.

They will lick dust like a snake, like creatures that crawl. They will come trembling from their dens, turn in fear to the Lord our God, afraid of you. Serpent imagery. The curse of Genesis 3:14 extended to the nations. Submission and fear before Israel's God.

Who is a God like you, who pardons sin and forgives the transgression of the remnant of his inheritance? You do not stay angry forever but delight to show mercy. Micah means 'Who is like Yahweh?' The book ends answering its own name. Divine uniqueness: mercy defines God. Anger passes; mercy delights.

You will again have compassion on us; you will tread our sins underfoot and hurl all our iniquities into the depths of the sea. Future compassion assured. Sins trampled like enemies. Iniquities drowned like Pharaoh's army. Total disposal of guilt.

You will be faithful to Jacob, show love to Abraham, as you pledged on oath to our ancestors in days long ago. The book closes with covenant affirmation. Jacob and Abraham invoked. Ancient oath fulfilled. What began in promise ends in faithfulness.
